source.title: Re-evaluating Circuit Mechanisms Underlying Pattern Separation

confidence_rationale: Included deliberately as the entry that constrains how far the other four can be pushed, and it earns its place by changing a design recommendation rather than merely adding caution. It supports the pull's central thesis -- that pattern separation is produced by STRUCTURAL circuit properties rather than by a downstream objective -- while reassigning which structural property matters: the authors argue the primary mechanism is expansion into a higher-dimensional space with SPARSE CONNECTIVITY, and that sparse ACTIVITY and lateral inhibition are secondary contributors rather than the core. That directly qualifies the Espinoza/Kim reading and it bears on the SD-016 design, because SD-016's retrieval layer is dimensionality-REDUCING (z_world dim 32 -> 16 slots) whereas every biological circuit reviewed here is strongly expansive. Direction is 'mixed' rather than 'supports' because the paper simultaneously strengthens the H2 leg and undercuts a naive H3-only reading. Confidence 0.74 reflects a high-quality synthesis review in a top venue by authors with the relevant modelling expertise, discounted because it is argument and synthesis rather than new measurement, and because its cross-circuit comparative frame (cerebellum, mushroom body, DG) means not every conclusion is hippocampus-specific.
failure_signatures: The paper's central structural claim is EXPANSION with sparse connectivity: cerebellar granule layer, insect mushroom body and dentate gyrus all map inputs into a much LARGER population than the input layer. SD-016 does the opposite -- it maps a 32-dim z_world onto 16 slots, a contraction. If expansion is the primary mechanism, then no choice of selection operator over 16 slots recovers it, and both H3 and H2 as currently scoped may be attacking a secondary variable. This is the single most consequential finding in this pull for the portfolio's design.

The authors explicitly state that recent findings 'have questioned long-held ideas' about how these circuits perform pattern separation -- so the Marr-lineage framing that the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy used as its biological reference is itself contested, and should not be treated as settled ground truth.

Decorrelation and sparse activity are argued to be neither necessary nor sufficient for pattern separation in general; a design that optimises a decorrelation/divergence metric (which is close to what SD-016's C1b context-divergence instrument measures) may improve the metric without improving the downstream associative-learning function the separation is FOR.

The relevant benefit of pattern separation in the authors' framing is facilitating associative learning IN THE PRESENCE OF TRIAL-TO-TRIAL VARIABILITY. SD-016's acceptance criteria (C1 entropy, C1b context-divergence) measure representational properties, not learning facilitation under noise, so a pass on both could still leave the functional benefit undemonstrated.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Recent findings have questioned long-held ideas about how the cerebellar cortex, insect mushroom body and dentate gyrus perform pattern separation. The authors argue that the dimensionality of the space available for population codes provides a common framework for understanding the computation, and that these three circuits use DIFFERENT strategies to separate activity patterns. Expansion of the input into a higher-dimensional representation via sparse, divergent connectivity is presented as the primary structural mechanism; sparse activity levels and lateral inhibition modulate but do not by themselves constitute pattern separation. The functional pay-off is framed as facilitating associative learning in the presence of trial-to-trial variability, rather than decorrelation as an end in itself.
mapping.ree_translation: This entry is the corrective on the other four, and it changes a recommendation rather than merely adding a caveat. It agrees with the pull's central thesis -- separation is structural, not loss-induced -- but reassigns the load-bearing structure from competition to EXPANSION. The consequence for SD-016 is direct and uncomfortable: extract_cue_context maps a 32-dimensional z_world onto 16 slots, a dimensionality CONTRACTION, whereas every circuit reviewed here is strongly expansive (the dentate gyrus has roughly tenfold more granule cells than its entorhinal input). If Cayco-Gajic and Silver are right that expansion with sparse connectivity is primary, then a competitive operator applied to 16 slots is being applied to a representation that has already been squeezed below the dimensionality where separation is achievable, and H3 may improve the entropy metric without fixing the underlying problem. This does not refute H3 -- an operator change is cheap, well-motivated by Espinoza, and worth running -- but it argues that the H2 (representation) leg should be scoped around SLOT-COUNT / EXPANSION as a first-class variable, not only around what a 'structured retrieval unit' looks like. Concretely: a slot-count ladder (16 / 64 / 256 with matched sparsity) is a cheap and directly-motivated H2 arm, and one the portfolio does not currently contain.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a synthesis review, not new measurement, and its comparative frame spans three phylogenetically distinct circuits (cerebellar granule layer, insect mushroom body, dentate gyrus) whose commonalities are the authors' argument rather than an established consensus -- so conclusions drawn here are not all hippocampus-specific. The expansion argument is strongest for the cerebellar granule layer, where the anatomy is most extreme, and the dentate gyrus is the case where the authors themselves note the most uncertainty. Two further limits on the REE translation: (i) 'dimensionality' in their sense is a property of the population CODE (how many independent directions the activity actually spans), not simply the unit count, so raising SD-016's slot count from 16 to 256 would not by itself produce expansion if the slots remain correlated -- the metric must be the effective dimensionality of the selection distributions, not the slot count; (ii) their functional criterion is associative learning under trial-to-trial variability, which SD-016's current C1/C1b instruments do not measure at all, so importing their framing honestly would mean adding an instrument, not just an arm.
mapping.source_context: Review/synthesis in Neuron covering cerebellar cortex, insect mushroom body and hippocampal dentate gyrus; draws on both experimental literature and the authors' own computational modelling of sparse expansive recoding.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron review by Cayco-Gajic and Silver, who are the relevant modelling authorities on sparse expansive recoding in the cerebellar granule layer; widely cited as the current re-framing of this literature. Source quality 0.85 rather than higher because it is synthesis and argument rather than new data. Mapping fidelity 0.72: the expansion-vs-contraction observation about SD-016 is a sharp and directly actionable mapping, but their notion of dimensionality is a property of the population code rather than of unit count, which complicates the naive 'add more slots' reading. Transfer risk 0.32 -- the cross-circuit comparative frame is itself an argument for domain-generality, which cuts the usual transfer worry, but the DG case is the one the authors treat most tentatively.
